meta.title: Oregon Trail: Westward
meta.notes: 30 sections (S01–S30) plus Good/Bad/Special endings. All endings loop to S01.
meta.blurb: You load a wagon, gather your family, and point west. The trail does not care why you travel—only whether you endure.

S01.text:
You stand at the edge of the eastern frontier with your family gathered close.

A covered wagon creaks under the weight of everything you own—and everything you hope to become.

The trail west stretches farther than you can see.

Somewhere beyond plains and rivers and graves lies Oregon.

Once you leave, turning back will not be easy.

S02.text:
The wagon rolls forward, wheels groaning like they already regret the decision.

The road east fades behind you, replaced by dust and grass.

Your family looks to you for reassurance.

You nod, even if you are not sure.

S03.text:
You take inventory.

Food is packed tight. Ammunition is counted twice. Spare parts are limited.

A cracked wagon wheel catches your eye.

It will hold—for now.

S04.text:
The days settle into rhythm: roll, stop, cook, sleep.

The land opens wide, beautiful and unforgiving.

You pass other wagons heading the same direction, each family carrying their own quiet fears.

S05.text:
You push the wagon hard.

The extra miles come at a cost.

One morning, the wheel gives out with a sharp crack.

The wagon lurches violently to one side.

S06.text:
Traveling together brings comfort and shared labor.

You trade stories around the fire at night.

One family warns you about bandits farther west.

S07.text:
You keep your distance from others.

The trail feels lonelier, but quieter.

At night, coyotes howl close enough to unsettle your children.

S08.text:
You spend a full day repairing the wheel.

Progress halts, but the wagon is sturdy again.

Your family rests, grateful for the pause.

S09.text:
You abandon the wagon, loading what you can onto your backs.

It is a desperate choice.

The trail does not forgive desperation.

S10.text:
The plains stretch endlessly.

You pass weathered grave markers—names, dates, warnings.

Each one reminds you what failure looks like.

choices.label: SAY A PRAYER AND MOVE ON

S11.text:
You ignore the warnings.

One night, shadows move near camp.

Bandits test your defenses, watching for weakness.

S12.text:
You rest longer than planned.

Illness moves through your family, slow but dangerous.

Rest may save them—or delay you into winter.

S13.text:
Your family regains strength.

The trail grows rockier as hills rise in the distance.

You feel both hope and dread.

S14.text:
You hunt and gather.

The land provides, but not without effort.

A rifle misfires, narrowly missing disaster.

S15.text:
You confront the bandits.

A tense standoff ends with them retreating, empty-handed.

Your supplies are intact—but nerves are frayed.

S16.text:
Pushing too hard takes its toll.

A family member collapses with fever.

You must decide between speed and survival.

S17.text:
You reach a wide river.

The current is fast and cold.

Other wagons lie broken along the bank.

S18.text:
You guide the wagon into the water.

The current pulls hard.

The wagon tilts dangerously.

S19.text:
You follow the river for days.

Time slips away, but you find a calmer crossing.

The delay weighs on your mind.

S20.text:
The wagon reaches the far bank.

Soaked but intact.

Your family cheers, exhausted and alive.

S21.text:
The land changes again—thick forests, steeper climbs.

Winter whispers in the wind.

S22.text:
You race the season.

Snow dusts the peaks ahead.

Every mile feels stolen from fate.

S23.text:
You slow your pace.

The safer path costs time but saves lives.

Food grows scarce.

S24.text:
The mountains give way to rolling green valleys.

The air smells different—cleaner.

Oregon is close.

S25.text:
You see fertile land stretching to the horizon.

Your family weeps with relief.

The journey has changed all of you.

S26.text:
You linger too long between choices.

Supplies dwindle.

The trail closes in around you.

S27.text:
A sudden storm batters the wagon.

You barely keep control.

S28.text:
You find an abandoned wagon.

Left behind. Supplies intact.

A silent gift—or a warning.

S29.text:
A child asks if the trail ever ends.

You don’t answer right away.

S30.text:
You look back at the miles behind you.

Graves. Rivers. Broken wheels.

You understand now: the trail was never about Oregon.

It was about who survived the journey.

END_GOOD.text:
GOOD ENDING — YOU MADE IT

You settle in Oregon.

The land is rich. The future uncertain.

But your family lives.

And that is enough.

END_BAD.text:
BAD ENDING — THE TRAIL CLAIMS YOU

The journey ends without ceremony.

The trail takes what it is owed.

Only weathered markers remain.

END_SPECIAL.text:
SPECIAL ENDING — THE JOURNEY CHANGED YOU

You survive—but you never truly arrive.

The road becomes part of who you are.

Home is no longer a place.
